paper.title: As We May Think
paper.author: Vannevar Bush
paper.description: 在个人电脑出现之前，设想一张可以储存资料、批注并连接阅读线索的书桌。
paper.note: 本站双语导读，非原文全文或逐句翻译。Memex 是设想中的机械化知识工具，不是已经实现的个人电脑。
paper.rights: 原文章受版权保护，本页仅提供本站编写的双语导读与来源链接。

glossary.memex: Memex（设想中的个人知识工具）

blocks.en: Bush imagines a personal device for keeping documents and following connections between them. The problem is how accumulated knowledge can remain usable for a working mind.
blocks.zh: 布什设想一种个人设备，用来保存资料，并沿着资料之间的联系阅读。问题在于：不断积累的知识，怎样才能持续为思考所用？

blocks.en: Memex combines storage, retrieval, annotation, and associative trails. Its proposed machinery belongs to its era, while the emphasis on connecting information remains recognizable.
blocks.zh: Memex 把存储、检索、批注和联想路径结合起来。设想中的机械装置属于它的时代，而把信息连接起来的思路，今天读来仍很熟悉。

blocks.en: The essay is especially relevant to a personal reading collection: saving an article is only one step. Recording why it connects to another article can preserve a line of thought.
blocks.zh: 这篇文章特别适合个人阅读收藏：保存文章只是一步。记录它为什么与另一篇文章相连，才能保存一条思考的线索。

blocks.en: Reading question: which relationships would you want your own archive to remember? Compare a collection organized by folders with one organized around questions and connections.
blocks.zh: 阅读时可以追问：你希望自己的资料库记住哪些关系？试着比较按文件夹整理的收藏，与围绕问题和联系组织的收藏。
